title: Checkpoint and resume long fits
text: Every nested-Laplace fitter takes control$checkpoint = list(path =, resume =). path checkpoint file; resume = TRUE reloads completed cells , resume = FALSE (default) starts fresh overwrites. grid cells now disk:
code: # A small nested-Laplace fit over an ICAR field on a chain graph. S <- 30L W <- matrix(0, S, S) for (i in 1:(S - 1)) W[i, i + 1] <- W[i + 1, i] <- 1 df <- data.frame(region = factor(seq_len(S))) df$x <- as.integer(df$region) / 10 + rnorm(S, 0, 0.3) df$y <- rbinom(S, 20, plogis(-0.4 + 0.5 * df$x))  ckpt <- tempfile(fileext = ".ckpt") fit <- tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = df, family = "binomial",              n_trials = rep(20L, S),              spatial = spatial_car(W, level = "obs"),              mode = "laplace",              control = list(checkpoint = list(path = ckpt, resume = FALSE))) coef(fit) file.exists(ckpt) && file.info(ckpt)$size > 0

code: periodic_ar1 <- function(n) {   tgmrf(     Q = function(theta) {       sigma <- exp(theta[1]); rho <- tanh(theta[2])       d <- rep((1 + rho^2) / sigma^2, n)       o <- rep(-rho / sigma^2, n)       M <- Matrix::bandSparse(n, k = c(-1, 0, 1),                               diagonals = list(o, d, o))       M[1, n] <- M[n, 1] <- -rho / sigma^2     # wrap       methods::as(methods::as(M, "generalMatrix"), "CsparseMatrix")     },     prior = function(theta) {       dnorm(theta[1], 0, 1, log = TRUE) +     # weak on log_sigma       dnorm(theta[2], 0, 1, log = TRUE)       # weak on atanh_rho     },     init   = c(log_sigma = 0, atanh_rho = atanh(0.3)),     bounds = list(lower = c(log(0.3), atanh(0.0)),                   upper = c(log(3.0), atanh(0.9))),     name   = "periodic_ar1"   ) }

code: n <- 40L theta_true <- c(log(0.8), atanh(0.6)) blk        <- periodic_ar1(n)  # z | theta_true ~ N(0, Q(theta_true)^{-1}) Q_true <- blk$Q(theta_true) L      <- Matrix::Cholesky(Q_true) z_true <- as.numeric(Matrix::solve(L, rnorm(n), system = "Lt"))  # y_i ~ Poisson(exp(beta_0 + z_i)) beta0 <- 0.3 y     <- rpois(n, exp(beta0 + z_true)) X     <- matrix(1, n, 1L)

code: library(tulpa)  # Poisson counts with a correlated site-level intercept and slope set.seed(1) site <- rep(seq_len(40), each = 8) x    <- rnorm(320) b0   <- rnorm(40, 0, 0.7)                          # site intercepts (truth SD 0.7) b1   <- rnorm(40, 0, 0.4)                          # site slopes     (truth SD 0.4) y    <- rpois(320, exp(0.2 + (0.5 + b1[site]) * x + b0[site])) d    <- data.frame(y, x, site = factor(site))  fit <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 + x | site), data = d, family = "poisson")  fit$selection_reason #> "random-slope term(s) present; RE covariance(s) integrated via re_cov_gibbs (1 block(s))"  summary(fit) #>             estimate  std.error    2.5%   97.5% #> (Intercept)    0.214      0.103  -0.003   0.401 #> x              0.488      0.087   0.322   0.658  fit$posterior          # the random-effect covariance, marginalized to sigma / rho #>   parameter    mean     sd   median   ci_lo   ci_hi #>     sigma_1   0.688  0.102    0.678   0.516   0.918   # intercept SD (truth 0.7) #>     sigma_2   0.469  0.074    0.461   0.345   0.636   # slope SD     (truth 0.4) #>      rho_12  -0.145  0.206   -0.156  -0.523   0.254   # correlation  (truth 0)

code: # Default: auto routes and records why on the fit fit <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 + x | site), data = d, family = "poisson") fit$selection_reason #> "random-slope term(s) present; RE covariance(s) integrated via re_cov_gibbs (1 block(s))"  # Same model, cheaper deterministic covariance integration (nested Laplace + CCD) fit <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 + x | site), data = d, family = "poisson",              control = list(re_cov = "nested")) fit$selection_reason #> "random-slope term(s) present; RE covariance(s) integrated via re_cov_nested (1 block(s))"  # Drop the correlation: an uncorrelated (diagonal) covariance block fit <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 + x || site), data = d, family = "poisson")

A directed neighbourhood cannot be represented by an undirected field.  # Use it in a model: graph stays explicit and inspectable # spatial(graph = g$adjacency, formula = ~ 1 || cell_idx)  # Remap observation data (original cell ids -> 1:n node indices) by key obs <- data.frame(cell = c("c5", "c1", "c5", "c9")) obs$cell_idx <- node_index(g, obs$cell) obs #>   cell cell_idx #> 1   c5        5 #> 2   c1        1 #> 3   c5        5 #> 4   c9        9

text: One entry per backend. Adding backend single entry ; tier membership, family support, input contract, R-level reachability derive list – single source truth per-tier backends family support. Fields: emits    – kind posterior representation backend's draws hold, fixes whether MCMC chain diagnostics apply (independent tier: exact SMC sampler emits "iid" particles, Tier-3 VI fit also emits "iid", nested-Laplace Tier-2 fit emits "iid" ): "chain" : autocorrelated MCMC output – Rhat autocorrelation-ESS meaningful (diagnostics() computes ). "iid"   : exchangeable draws deterministic approximation, resampled particles – split-Rhat vacuous ESS = n construction, say nothing approximation bias. "point" : posterior sample (mode + covariance ). tier     – tier key ("exact", "structured", "optimized"). input    – input contract backend's fitter consumes: "design"    : design-matrix bundle (y, n_trials, X, RE structure). "logpost"   : log_posterior(theta) closure plus dimension/init. "modeldata" : tulpa ModelData / LikelihoodSpec (C-ABI NUTS path). "nested"    : design-matrix bundle plus one latent prior blocks (latent(tgmrf(...))), integrated block hyperparameters nested-Laplace driver. "spde"      : design bundle plus self-contained SPDE spec (mesh + FEM matrices); fit_spde()'s CCD / grid hyperparameter engine. fitter   – name R function implementing backend, NULL C++ kernel exists R entry point yet. Stored string (function object) registry independent source-load order; resolved lazily via resolve_backend_fitter(). NULL => selectable R; dispatch fails loudly. families – character vector supported family identifiers, NULL unrestricted backend. cabi     – registered C-ABI callable backing backend (symbol model package reaches via LinkingTo: tulpa, one R wrapper call), NULL. note     – optional human-readable note. what: Central Composite Design (CCD) grid for nested-Laplace integration — ccd_grid
title: Central Composite Design (CCD) grid for nested-Laplace integration — ccd_grid
text: Produces structured set standardised hyperparameter points \(z \\mathbb{R}^k\) use integration nodes nested Laplace approximation \(k \ge 3\). CCD scales much better full tensor expand.grid() used 1D 2D backends: CCD \(1 + 2k + 2^{k - q}\) points (1 centre, 2k axial, \(2^{k - q}\) factorial), versus \(m^k\) m-per-axis tensor product. Point layout (centre+axial+factorial scaling \(f_0\)): 1 centre point origin; 2k axial points \(\pm f_0\) along coordinate axis; \(2^{k - q}\) factorial points corners hypercube, scaled lie sphere radius \(f_0\). \(k \le 6\) factorial portion full \(2^k\) design. \(k \ge 7\) half-fraction (\(q = 1\)) using defining word \(x_1 \cdots x_k\) keeps point count reasonable preserving Resolution V. Used tulpa_nested_laplace() higher-dimensional hyperparameter blocks. standardised z-coordinates mapped physical hyperparameters \(\theta\) via ccd_to_theta().

Pass diag(sd) diagonal axis-aligned grid sd per-axis posterior SD; pass Cholesky factor capture correlations hyperparameters. log_scale Logical (logical vector length k). what: Corrected R-INLA CCD integration weights — ccd_weights
title: Corrected R-INLA CCD integration weights — ccd_weights
text: Per-point design weights ccd_grid() used nested-Laplace integration nodes. Implements corrected R-INLA central-composite-design weights: formula Rue, Martino Chopin (2009) typo, corrected R-INLA team give positive central weight. m hyperparameters, np design points standardized scaling f0, every non-centre point gets $$w = 1 / ((np - 1)(1 + e^{-m f0^2 / 2}(f0^2 - 1)))$$ centre point gets \(w_0 = 1 - (np - 1) w\). Used \(\Delta_k\): integration weight node \(k\) \(\Delta_k \exp(\log\,\mathrm{marginal}_k)\), renormalized. standardized (whitened) hyperparameter posterior reproduce Gaussian moments exactly.

title: Inference Mode System — inference_modes
text: tulpa uses explicit tier system inference encodes epistemic guarantees, just runtime characteristics. design makes difference inference methods first-class unavoidable, rather hiding implementation details.

title: Inference Mode System — inference_modes
text: Tier 1 - Exact: Asymptotically correct posterior inference (Monte Carlo error). Credible intervals interpretable posterior uncertainty. reference standard. Tier 2 - Structured: Accurate inference conditional explicit structural assumptions. Typically requires latent Gaussian structure, conditional independence, smooth posteriors. fast right model class, can wrong outside class. Failure modes predictable explainable. Tier 3 - Optimized: general correctness guarantee beyond empirical usefulness. Point estimates usually good, uncertainty often underestimated. Tails correlations unreliable. Failure usually silent. optimization, sampling.

title: Create a latent factor specification — latent_factor
text: modeling multiple processes, often share unmeasured confounders. example, relative abundance data, focal species count total count might affected : Observer skill (unmeasured) Local microhabitat conditions (unmeasured) Weather sampling day (unmeasured) Without accounting shared drivers, estimates can biased. Latent factors capture shared structure without requiring confounders measured.

title: Create a latent factor specification — latent_factor
text: observation K latent factors, two model arms (processes 1 2): $$\eta^{(1)}_i = X^{(1)}_i \beta^{(1)} + \sum_{k=1}^{K} f_{ik} \sigma_k + \ldots$$ $$\eta^{(2)}_i = X^{(2)}_i \beta^{(2)} + \sum_{k=1}^{K} f_{ik} \sigma_k + \ldots$$ : \(f_{ik} \sim N(0, 1)\) standardized factor scores \(\sigma_k\) factor standard deviations PC prior Identifiability: \(\sum_i f_{ik} = 0\) k factors enter linear predictors identically (shared), cancel derived quantities (e.g., ratios, differences): $$\eta^{(1)}_i - \eta^{(2)}_i$$ means factors capture shared effects otherwise bias derived quantities.

title: Create a latent factor specification — latent_factor
text: Start n_factors = 1 simple unmeasured confounding Use n_factors = 2-3 suspect multiple independent confounders 3 factors rarely needed risks overfitting PC prior provides regularization, shrinking unneeded factors toward zero

title: Create a latent factor specification — latent_factor
text: Latent factors differ random effects several ways: Random effects grouped (e.g., site-level), factors observation-level Random effects require grouping structure, factors Factors capture residual correlation explained observed predictors can use together: random effects known grouping, factors residual unmeasured confounding.

title: Create a latent factor specification — latent_factor
code: # Basic latent factor (single shared factor) latent_factor() #> Latent factor specification #> =========================== #>  #> Number of factors: 1  #> Shared: Yes (enters all processes)  #> Constraint: sum_to_zero  #> Scale: Yes  #>  #> Factor SD prior: #>   PC prior: P(x > 1.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(4.605)  # Two latent factors latent_factor(n_factors = 2) #> Latent factor specification #> =========================== #>  #> Number of factors: 2  #> Shared: Yes (enters all processes)  #> Constraint: sum_to_zero  #> Scale: Yes  #>  #> Factor SD prior: #>   PC prior: P(x > 1.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(4.605)  # Custom prior (more regularization) latent_factor(n_factors = 1, prior = prior_pc(U = 0.5, alpha = 0.01)) #> Latent factor specification #> =========================== #>  #> Number of factors: 1  #> Shared: Yes (enters all processes)  #> Constraint: sum_to_zero  #> Scale: Yes  #>  #> Factor SD prior: #>   PC prior: P(x > 0.50) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(9.210)  # Numerator-only factor (not shared) latent_factor(n_factors = 1, shared = FALSE) #> Latent factor specification #> =========================== #>  #> Number of factors: 1  #> Shared: No (first process only)  #> Constraint: sum_to_zero  #> Scale: Yes  #>  #> Factor SD prior: #>   PC prior: P(x > 1.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(4.605)  # The spec is consumed by a ratio / multi-arm model package (tulpaRatio owns # the two-arm `species | total ~ ...` formula and the negbin/negbin ratio # family); it is that package's fitter, not the single-response tulpa() front # door, that reads the `latent_factor()` object.

title: Metropolis-Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA) — mala
text: Sample posterior using MALA: Langevin proposal driven gradient log posterior, corrected Metropolis- Hastings accept/reject step. iteration one log-posterior + one gradient evaluation. natural stepping stone random-walk MH HMC: cheaper per iteration HMC (leapfrog integration), better-mixing RWMH drift term moves toward higher density. Step size epsilon adapted via dual averaging warmup target acceptance rate 0.574 (Roberts & Rosenthal 1998 optimal high-dimensional Gaussians).

title: Metropolis-Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA) — mala
code: mala(   log_posterior,   grad_log_posterior,   init,   n_iter = 2000L,   warmup = n_iter%/%2L,   epsilon = 0.1,   target_accept = 0.574,   mass_diag = NULL,   thin = 1L,   verbose = FALSE )

title: Metropolis-Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA) — mala
text: log_posterior Function function(theta) -> numeric returning unnormalized log posterior. grad_log_posterior Function function(theta) -> numeric vector returning gradient theta. init Numeric vector: initial state (must give finite log_posterior). n_iter Total iterations including warmup (default 2000). warmup Warmup iterations (step-size adaptation + discarded; default n_iter / 2). epsilon Initial step size (default 0.1). Adapted warmup. target_accept Target acceptance warmup adaptation (default 0.574, Roberts & Rosenthal 1998 optimum). mass_diag Optional preconditioner: length-d vector per-dimension variances, used diagonal inverse-mass M^-1. proposal N(theta + (eps^2/2) * M^-1 * grad, eps^2 * M^-1), entry j scales proposal variance along dimension j noise standard deviation eps * sqrt(mass_diag[j]). Default rep(1, d). posteriors different scales across dimensions, set (estimate ) posterior variances, .e. squared posterior SDs. thin Keep every thin-th post-warmup sample (default 1). verbose Print acceptance + step-size summary end (default FALSE).

title: Show default priors for a tulpa family — priors_default
text: Default priors tulpa follow principles: Fixed effects (beta): Normal(0, 2.5) - weakly informative, allows coefficients roughly [-5, 5] link scale. Random effect SD (sigma): PC prior P(sigma > 1) = 0.01 - favors simpler models smaller variance components. Overdispersion (phi): PC prior P(phi > 10) = 0.01 NB2 size phi (larger phi less overdispersion; phi -> Inf Poisson limit). default keeps phi finite, allowing overdispersion penalising extreme values. Temporal correlation (rho): Beta(2, 2) - symmetric prior centered 0.5, appropriate AR(1) correlation. Spatial mixing (rho_spatial): Beta(1, 1) = Uniform(0, 1) - prior preference structured vs. unstructured spatial variation.

title: Show default priors for a tulpa family — priors_default
code: # Defaults for all families (no family argument) priors_default() #> Default priors for tulpa models #> ================================ #>  #> These defaults apply to all families unless overridden. #>  #> Fixed effects (beta): #>   Normal(0, 2.5) #>   Interpretation: Coefficients roughly in [-5, 5] on link scale #>   Customization: prior_normal(mean, sd) #>  #> Random effect SD (sigma): #>   PC prior: P(sigma > 1) = 0.01 #>   Interpretation: Favors smaller variance components #>   Customization: prior_pc(U, alpha) or prior_half_normal(sd) #>  #> Overdispersion (phi) [negbin/poisson_gamma only]: #>   PC prior: P(phi > 10) = 0.01 #>   Interpretation: NB2 size; keeps phi finite (allows overdispersion), #>                   phi -> Inf is the Poisson limit #>   Customization: prior_pc(U, alpha) or prior_gamma(shape, rate) #>  #> Family-specific notes: #>   negbin_negbin: Uses phi for both processes #>   binomial: No overdispersion parameter (unless beta_binomial) #>   poisson_gamma: Uses phi for gamma shape parameter  # Family-specific defaults take a tulpa_family object. Model packages # (e.g. tulpaRatio) register rich families; a minimal one is enough here. fam <- tulpa_family(   name = "poisson_gamma",   simulate_fn = function(eta, params, n_obs, ...) rpois(n_obs, exp(eta[[1]])) ) priors_default(fam) #> Default priors for poisson_gamma family #> =====================================  #>  #> Fixed effects (beta): #>   Normal(0.00, 2.50) #>   Used for: All regression coefficients in all processes #>  #> Random effect SD (sigma): #>   PC prior: P(x > 1.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(4.605) #>   Used for: Standard deviation of group-level effects #>  #> Overdispersion (phi): #>   PC prior: P(x > 10.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(0.461) #>   Used for: Gamma shape parameter for effort/exposure #>  #> To customize, use tulpa_priors(): #>   priors <- tulpa_priors( #>     beta = prior_normal(0, 1), #>     sigma = prior_pc(U = 0.5, alpha = 0.01) #>   )  # Including spatial parameters priors_default(fam, spatial = TRUE) #> Default priors for poisson_gamma family #> =====================================  #>  #> Fixed effects (beta): #>   Normal(0.00, 2.50) #>   Used for: All regression coefficients in all processes #>  #> Random effect SD (sigma): #>   PC prior: P(x > 1.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(4.605) #>   Used for: Standard deviation of group-level effects #>  #> Overdispersion (phi): #>   PC prior: P(x > 10.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(0.461) #>   Used for: Gamma shape parameter for effort/exposure #>  #> Spatial mixing (rho_spatial): #>   Beta(1.00, 1.00)  [mean = 0.50] #>   Used for: BYM2 mixing proportion (structured vs. unstructured) #>  #> To customize, use tulpa_priors(): #>   priors <- tulpa_priors( #>     beta = prior_normal(0, 1), #>     sigma = prior_pc(U = 0.5, alpha = 0.01) #>   )  # Use as a starting point for customization my_priors <- priors_default(fam) #> Default priors for poisson_gamma family #> =====================================  #>  #> Fixed effects (beta): #>   Normal(0.00, 2.50) #>   Used for: All regression coefficients in all processes #>  #> Random effect SD (sigma): #>   PC prior: P(x > 1.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(4.605) #>   Used for: Standard deviation of group-level effects #>  #> Overdispersion (phi): #>   PC prior: P(x > 10.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(0.461) #>   Used for: Gamma shape parameter for effort/exposure #>  #> To customize, use tulpa_priors(): #>   priors <- tulpa_priors( #>     beta = prior_normal(0, 1), #>     sigma = prior_pc(U = 0.5, alpha = 0.01) #>   ) my_priors$beta <- prior_normal(0, 1)  # code: # A conjugate normal-normal model, whose posterior is exact, so its PIT must # be uniform: the harness scoring itself. sim <- function(seed) {   set.seed(seed)   mu <- rnorm(1)   list(y = rnorm(10L, mu, 1), theta = c(mu = mu)) } fitter <- function(d) {   v <- 1 / (1 + length(d$y))   list(exact  = list(mu = sbc_normal(v * sum(d$y), sqrt(v))),        narrow = list(mu = sbc_normal(v * sum(d$y), sqrt(v) / 2))) } res <- sbc("prior_predictive", simulator = sim, fitter = fitter, n_sim = 60L) res #> Simulation-based calibration -- prior_predictive, 60 simulations #>   band: 0.95 simultaneous (equal local levels, exact crossing probability) #>   CRPS: proper posterior score #>   proper prior: verified over 10 probed simulations #>  #>     arm quantity  n     ks inside   p_unif inside_folded p_folded    crps #>   exact       mu 60 0.1239   TRUE 1.72e-01          TRUE    0.466 0.19496 #>  narrow       mu 60 0.2662  FALSE 1.22e-15         FALSE    0.000 0.21762 #>  crps_se #>   0.0166 #>   0.0215 #>  #> 1 of 2 (arm, quantity) reads inside the band; outside the band: narrow/mu. summary(res, baseline = "exact") #> Simulation-based calibration -- prior_predictive, 60 simulations #>   CRPS: proper posterior score #>  #>     arm quantity  n     ks inside   p_unif inside_folded p_folded    crps #>   exact       mu 60 0.1239   TRUE 1.72e-01          TRUE    0.466 0.19496 #>  narrow       mu 60 0.2662  FALSE 1.22e-15         FALSE    0.000 0.21762 #>  crps_se #>   0.0166 #>   0.0215 #>  #> Paired CRPS against arm 'exact' (negative delta = better) #>  quantity    arm  n   delta   t worse_frac p_sign #>        mu narrow 60 0.02267 4.3      0.633 0.0519 #>   delta with its t is the proper-score verdict; p_sign is a more #>   powerful detector of a difference but is not itself proper.

title: Areal spatially varying coefficient field — spatial
text: graph Symmetric adjacency matrix spatial graph ([n_node x n_node], dense sparse). One CAR field defined nodes per coefficient. formula One-sided formula carrying grouping bar, e.g. ~ 1 + time || cell. left-hand side expanded stats::model.matrix() one CAR field per column (1 = intercept field; covariate = spatially varying slope ; 0 + drops intercept). right-hand side must single bare column naming graph node. double bar || builds independent fields (precision); single bar | builds correlated fields – separable multivariate CAR per-cell coefficient vector shares cross-covariance Sigma (covariance Sigma (x) Q^-1), intercept-slope correlation rho shared across graph. proper Logical; FALSE (default) builds intrinsic CAR (ICAR / Besag) fields sum--zero constraint (rho fixed 1). TRUE builds proper CAR fields, precision Q = D - rho_car W spatial autocorrelation rho_car estimated data (one (sigma, rho_car) pair per field). summary() print() report per-field rho_car. Independent (||) ; correlated proper CAR (single | proper = TRUE) separate model. shared Optional shared-effect handle, passed field blocks (see model docs). Default NULL (shared). Optional replicated-CAR factor: bare column name (string) naming factor model data. L levels builds one independent copy whole field per level – field block-diagonal Kronecker graph I_L (x) Q (L disjoint copies graph) – hyperparameters shared across levels (one Sigma |; one (sigma[, rho_car]) ||). INLA's replicate = / mgcv's s(cell, = ...) generalised varying-coefficient bar, orthogonal bar character: | / || sets covariance among coefficient columns within field, sets many independent replicates whole field exist. code: # Create adjacency matrix for 10 regions (chain structure) adj <- matrix(0, 10, 10) for (i in 1:9) {   adj[i, i+1] <- adj[i+1, i] <- 1 }  # Create BYM2 spatial structure bym2 <- spatial_bym2(adj, level = "group", group_var = "region") print(bym2) #> tulpa spatial specification #> =========================== #>  #> Type: BYM2  #> Level: group  #> Spatial units: 10  #> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)  #> Group variable: region  #> Scale factor: 0.8169   # \donttest{ # Disease mapping with BYM2 spatial smoothing set.seed(456) n_regions <- 10 epi_data <- data.frame(   region = factor(rep(1:n_regions, each = 4)),   age = rnorm(n_regions * 4, 50, 10) ) epi_data$cases <- rbinom(nrow(epi_data), size = 100, prob = 0.15)  fit <- tulpa(   cases ~ age + spatial(region),   spatial = spatial_bym2(adj, level = "group", group_var = "region"),   data = epi_data,   family = "binomial",   n_trials = rep(100L, nrow(epi_data)),   mode = "laplace" ) summary(fit) #>                 estimate   std.error         2.5%       97.5% #> (Intercept) -1.957897801 0.378119249 -2.698997911 -1.21679769 #> age          0.006390932 0.004661451 -0.002745343  0.01552721 # }

Default: c("local", "regional"). approx Approximation method: "nngp" (default) Nearest Neighbor GP; "hsgp" Hilbert Space GP (faster smooth fields). m Number HSGP basis functions per dimension (default 6). used approx = "hsgp". Total basis functions m^2. c_boundary Boundary factor HSGP domain extension (default 1.5). used approx = "hsgp". range_local Plausible range interval local scale c(lower, upper) coordinate units. Default: c(0.01, 1) (scaling). exact NUTS hard box: lower anchors PC prior scale's range (P(range < lower) = 0.05, prior spatial_gp() uses), pair places sampler's starting range geometric mean. range free (0, Inf). range_regional Plausible range interval regional scale, read way. Default: c(1, 10) (scaling). Keeping two intervals separated identifies scales . cov Covariance function: "exponential" (default) "matern". nu Smoothness parameter Matern covariance, one 1.5 2.5. nn_local Number nearest neighbors local scale. Default 10. nn_regional Number nearest neighbors regional scale. Default 30. shared Logical; TRUE (default), spatial effects enter processes. scale_coords Logical; TRUE (default), coordinates scaled unit variance computing distances. sampler Latent parameterization exact-NUTS field. "auto" (default) "noncentered" sample z ~ N(0, ) per scale reconstruct field w = f(z, sigma2, phi), avoiding field/hyperparameter funnel; "centered" places NNGP density field directly. "interweaved" alternates parameterizations implemented exact-NUTS path.

text: tulpa_multiscale object

title: Multi-Scale Gaussian Process spatial structure — spatial_multiscale
text: multi-scale model decomposes spatial variation additively: $$\eta(s) = X\beta + w_{local}(s) + w_{regional}(s)$$ component follows independent Gaussian process: $$w_{local}(s) \sim GP(0, \sigma^2_{local} C(\phi_{local}))$$ $$w_{regional}(s) \sim GP(0, \sigma^2_{regional} C(\phi_{regional}))$$ Identifiability: sufficient data (>500 locations), two scales typically well-identified prior ranges non-overlapping. PC priors variance components help prevent overfitting. Computational cost: Approximately 1.5-2x cost single-scale GP, two NNGP likelihoods must evaluated.

title: Multi-Scale Gaussian Process spatial structure — spatial_multiscale
code: # Create multi-scale spatial structure ms <- spatial_multiscale(   ~ lon + lat,   range_local = c(0.1, 0.5),   range_regional = c(1, 5) ) print(ms) #> tulpa Multi-Scale spatial specification #> ======================================== #>  #> Coordinates: lon, lat  #> Scales: local + regional  #>  #> Local scale: #>   Range prior: [0.1, 0.5] #>   Neighbors: 10  #>  #> Regional scale: #>   Range prior: [1, 5] #>   Neighbors: 30  #>  #> Covariance: exponential  #> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)   if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ set.seed(101) n <- 60 df <- data.frame(   lon = runif(n, 0, 10),   lat = runif(n, 0, 10),   depth = rnorm(n),   temp = rnorm(n) ) df$count <- rpois(n, exp(1 + 0.2 * df$depth))  # Both scales are sampled by exact NUTS (mode = "exact"); the field is # returned as gp_local[i] / gp_regional[i] draws. fit <- tulpa(   count ~ depth + temp,   data = df,   family = "poisson",   spatial = spatial_multiscale(     ~ lon + lat,     range_local = c(0.1, 0.5),     range_regional = c(1, 5)   ),   mode = "exact",   control = list(n_iter = 200L, n_warmup = 100L) ) summary(fit) } # }

code: # Create RSR spatial structure rsr <- spatial_rsr(   spatial_gp(~ lon + lat),   restrict_to = ~ depth + temp ) print(rsr) #> tulpa Gaussian Process spatial specification #> ============================================= #>  #> Coordinates: lon, lat  #> Covariance: exponential  #> Neighbors (NNGP): 15  #> Solver: auto (Cholesky<2k, PCG<5k, GPU/CG for larger)  #> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)  #>  #> Restricted Spatial Regression (RSR): #>   Orthogonal to: ~depth + temp  #>   (Spatial effect constrained to be orthogonal to covariate space)  # \donttest{ # Areal binomial data on a chain of regions, covariate spatially confounded set.seed(404) n_regions <- 12 W <- matrix(0, n_regions, n_regions) for (i in 1:(n_regions - 1)) W[i, i + 1] <- W[i + 1, i] <- 1 df <- data.frame(region = factor(rep(1:n_regions, each = 5))) df$x <- as.integer(df$region) / 4 + rnorm(nrow(df), 0, 0.5) df$y <- rbinom(nrow(df), 20, plogis(-0.5 + 0.6 * df$x))  # RSR orthogonalises the spatial field to x, protecting its coefficient fit <- tulpa(   y ~ x + spatial(region),   data = df,   family = "binomial",   n_trials = rep(20L, nrow(df)),   spatial = spatial_rsr(spatial_car(W, level = "obs"), restrict_to = ~ x),   mode = "auto",   control = list(n_iter = 500L, warmup = 250L) ) summary(fit) #>               estimate  std.error       2.5%       97.5% #> (Intercept) -0.3041358 0.11279820 -0.5456689 -0.07648903 #> x            0.5197550 0.06365316  0.4031921  0.64072967 # }

title: Spatiotemporal interaction specifications for tulpa — spatiotemporal
text: Spatiotemporal interactions extend basic additive model: $$\eta_{st} = X\beta + f_s(space) + f_t(time)$$ include interactions: $$\eta_{st} = X\beta + f_s(space) + f_t(time) + \delta_{st}$$ \(\delta_{st}\) captures space-time interactions. Interaction Types (following Knorr-Held, 2000): Type : Unstructured interaction - IID \(\delta_{st} \sim N(0, \sigma^2)\) Type II: Structured time, unstructured space - temporal structure location Type III: Structured space, unstructured time - spatial structure time Type IV: Structured space time - full Kronecker interaction Separable Models: Separable: Covariance Kronecker product \(C_{st} = C_s \otimes C_t\) Non-separable: GP joint space-time metric Type (IID) Independent random effect space-time combination: $$\delta_{st} \stackrel{iid}{\sim} N(0, \sigma^2_\delta)$$ simplest form, requiring S*T parameters capturing structured interaction. Type II (Temporal structure per location) location temporal random effect: $$\delta_{\cdot t}^{(s)} \sim RW(\sigma^2)$$ captures location-specific temporal trends assumes independence across locations. Type III (Spatial structure per time point) time point spatial random effect: $$\delta_{s \cdot}^{(t)} \sim ICAR(\tau)$$ captures time-specific spatial patterns assumes independence across time points. Type IV (Full structure) Kronecker product spatial temporal precision matrices: $$Q_\delta = Q_s \otimes Q_t$$ constrained model, assuming interaction structure marginal effects. Separable GP-based effects, assumes separable covariance: $$C(\mathbf{s}_1, t_1; \mathbf{s}_2, t_2) = C_s(\mathbf{s}_1, \mathbf{s}_2) \cdot C_t(t_1, t_2)$$

title: AR(2) temporal latent field (second-order autoregressive) — temporal_ar2
text: stationary second-order autoregressive process \(w_t = \phi_1 w_{t-1} + \phi_2 w_{t-2} + \varepsilon_t\) user-defined GMRF latent block, use model formula via latent(temporal_ar2(...)). reuses tulpa's nested-Laplace / NUTS machinery (dedicated C++ kernel). precision exact stationary AR(2) GMRF; stationarity enforced PACF parameterization, hyperparameter grid never leaves stationarity region. block's hyperparameters log_tau (log innovation precision) atanh_psi1, atanh_psi2 (unconstrained partial autocorrelations); AR coefficients recovered phi2 = tanh(atanh_psi2), phi1 = tanh(atanh_psi1) (1 - phi2).

title: Gaussian Process temporal structure — temporal_gp
text: time_var Name time variable data. Can formula (e.g., ~ year) character string (e.g., "year"). numeric (continuous time) convertible numeric. cov Covariance function: "exponential" (default, rough), "matern" (tunable smoothness), "gaussian" (smooth), "periodic" (seasonal patterns). nu Smoothness parameter Matern covariance, one : 0.5: equivalent exponential (rough) 1.5: differentiable (moderate smoothness) 2.5: twice differentiable (smooth) smoothnesses closed form; anything needs Bessel function second kind rejected. Ignored non-Matern covariance functions. period Period periodic covariance (e.g., 12 monthly, 365 daily data annual cycle). used cov = "periodic". group_var Optional name grouping variable panel data. provided, separate GPs estimated group. shared Logical; TRUE (default), temporal effect enters processes. scale_coords Logical; TRUE (default), time values scaled unit variance computing distances. parameterization Parameterization GP effects: "noncentered" (default) stores z ~ N(0,1) scales covariance (better weakly-informed effects); "centered" stores effects directly (better strongly-informed effects).

title: Gaussian Process temporal structure — temporal_gp
text: GP temporal model adds time-correlated random effect: $$\eta(t) = X\beta + f(t)$$ \(f(t)\) follows Gaussian process: $$f(t) \sim GP(0, \sigma^2 C(|t - t'|; \phi))$$ correlation function \(C(d; \phi)\) depends time distance \(d\): Exponential: \(C(d) = \exp(-d/\phi)\) - continuous differentiable Matern: Smooth tunable roughness via \(\nu\) Gaussian: \(C(d) = \exp(-(d/\phi)^2)\) - infinitely differentiable Periodic: \(C(d) = \exp(-2\sin^2(\pi d/p)/\phi^2)\) - seasonal data Implementation: exponential kernel (equivalently Matern nu = 0.5) Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, joint density factorizes first-order Markov chain evaluates O(T) matrix. kernels finite-dimensional state-space form evaluated dense T x T Cholesky, T number distinct time points. field fit sampler path: two hyperparameters (log_sigma2_temporal_gp, logit_phi_temporal_gp) sampled jointly field fixed effects, pass sampler mode mode = "hmc". nested-Laplace kernel .

title: Gaussian Process temporal structure — temporal_gp
code: # Create GP temporal specification temporal_gp("timestamp") #> tulpa Gaussian Process temporal specification #> ============================================== #>  #> Time variable: timestamp  #> Covariance: exponential  #> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)  temporal_gp("day", cov = "matern", nu = 1.5) #> tulpa Gaussian Process temporal specification #> ============================================== #>  #> Time variable: day  #> Covariance: matern (nu = 1.5)  #> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)  temporal_gp("month", cov = "periodic", period = 12) #> tulpa Gaussian Process temporal specification #> ============================================== #>  #> Time variable: month  #> Covariance: periodic (period = 12.0)  #> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)   # \donttest{ # Irregularly-spaced time series set.seed(140) times <- sort(runif(40, 0, 10)) df <- data.frame(   time = times,   x = rnorm(40),   y = rbinom(40, 1, 0.5) )  fit <- tulpa(   y ~ x,   data = df,   family = "binomial",   temporal = temporal_gp("time"),   mode = "hmc",   control = list(n_iter = 200, warmup = 100, n_chains = 1) ) # }

title: User-defined GMRF latent block — tgmrf
text: tgmrf() lets user define Gaussian Markov random field latent block tulpa model supplying two R closures: precision-matrix factory Q(theta) log-prior theta prior(theta). resulting object plugs formula via latent(tgmrf(...)) consumed every tulpa inference tier (Laplace, EM+Laplace, VI, nested_laplace+CCD, NUTS, IMH-Laplace). latent-side dual LikelihoodSpec. LikelihoodSpec lets model package observation model; tgmrf() lets script single latent block.

title: User-defined GMRF latent block — tgmrf
text: Q function function(theta) returning sparse precision matrix class Matrix::sparseMatrix (typically dgCMatrix). matrix must square symmetric. Called registration theta = init infer n_latent capture sparsity pattern. prior function function(theta) returning finite numeric scalar – log-prior density theta. init Numeric vector starting values theta. Names, present, become canonical theta names. mu Optional function function(theta) returning numeric vector length n_latent. Default NULL equivalent zero mean. graph Optional sparse matrix specifying upper bound Q's sparsity pattern. supplied, registration check verifies nonzero pattern Q(init) subset. bounds Optional list components lower upper, numeric vector length length(init). Used nested_laplace + CCD build outer grid; unused NUTS / VI. obs_idx Optional integer vector mapping observation latent slot [1, n_latent]. NULL (default), fit-time driver assumes N == n_latent uses seq_len(N) – .e. one observation per latent slot, row order. name Optional character; cosmetic label used print() / summary().

title: User-defined GMRF latent block — tgmrf
text: object class c("tgmrf", "tulpa_latent_block") components: Q, prior, mu – user closures (NULL mu). init, theta_names, theta_dim – hyperparameter metadata. n_latent – inferred Q(init). pattern – captured sparsity pattern dgCMatrix 1s. graph – user-supplied pattern, validated pattern given. bounds, name – passed .

title: User-defined GMRF latent block — tgmrf
text: Gaussian latent block z ~ N(mu(theta), Q(theta)^{-1}): $$\log p(z\mid\theta) = \tfrac{1}{2}\log\det Q(\theta) - \tfrac{1}{2}(z - \mu(\theta))^\top Q(\theta)(z - \mu(\theta)) + \mathrm{const}$$ gradient -Q(z - mu) Hessian -Q wrt z closed form, user never writes gradient code. Laplace inner step needs Q(theta) mu(theta) numeric theta. NUTS VI additionally use forward finite-difference gradient theta, costing dim(theta) extra Q calls per outer step – cheap typical dim(theta) <= 5.

title: User-defined GMRF latent block — tgmrf
code: # Periodic AR(1) block, wrap-around tridiagonal precision. periodic_ar1 <- function(n) {   tgmrf(     Q = function(theta) {       sigma <- exp(theta[1]); rho <- tanh(theta[2])       d <- rep((1 + rho^2) / sigma^2, n)       o <- rep(-rho / sigma^2, n)       M <- Matrix::bandSparse(         n, k = c(-1, 0, 1), diagonals = list(o, d, o)       )       M[1, n] <- M[n, 1] <- -rho / sigma^2       methods::as(M, "CsparseMatrix")     },     prior = function(theta) {       stats::dnorm(theta[1], 0, 1, log = TRUE) +         stats::dnorm(theta[2], 0, 1, log = TRUE)     },     init = c(log_sigma = 0, atanh_rho = 0),     name = "periodic_ar1"   ) }  blk <- periodic_ar1(20) print(blk) #> <tgmrf> "periodic_ar1" #>   n_latent : 20 #>   theta    : 2 dim (log_sigma, atanh_rho) #>   init     : 0, 0 #>   Q nnz    : 20 (5% of dense) #>   backend  : r

what: tulpa: Template Unified Latent Process Architecture for Bayesian Hierarchical Models — tulpa-package
title: tulpa: Template Unified Latent Process Architecture for Bayesian Hierarchical Models — tulpa-package
text: general-purpose engine fitting Bayesian hierarchical models spatial fields, temporal effects, spatially varying coefficients, multiple inference backends. Scalable spatial structure includes Hilbert space approximate Gaussian processes (HSGP; Riutort-Mayol et al. 2023 doi:10.1007/s11222-022-10167-2 ), nearest-neighbor Gaussian processes (NNGP; Datta et al. 2016 doi:10.1080/01621459.2015.1044091 ), intrinsic conditional autoregressive models (ICAR; Besag, York, Mollie 1991 doi:10.1007/BF00116466 ), reparameterized Besag-York-Mollie model (BYM2; Riebler et al. 2016 doi:10.1177/0962280216660421 ), stochastic partial differential equation fields (SPDE; Lindgren, Rue, Lindstrom 2011 doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2011.00777.x ). Temporal structure covers random walks, autoregressive processes, Gaussian processes. Inference tiered correctness guarantee: exact Hamiltonian Monte Carlo -U-Turn sampler, Laplace nested Laplace approximations hyperparameter integration (Rue, Martino, Chopin 2009 doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2008.00700.x ), variational inference. Model-specific packages plug observation likelihoods engine templated C++ callback interface.

Backends without phi2 channel refuse rather fit family's default. estimate_phi covers phi alone; phi2 always conditioned . beta_prior Optional list(mean, sd) Gaussian prior fixed effects. re_prior Optional list() random-effect / variance-component hyperpriors (statistical, live signature rather control). Available count families compiled zero-inflated kernel; paired truncated_poisson truncated_neg_binomial_2 hurdle model, since base P(Y = 0) 0 mixture degenerates two-part likelihood. Backends carry mixture refuse rather fit model without . zi_prior Optional list(sd) Gaussian prior zero-inflation coefficients, beta_zi ~ N(0, sd^2); NULL (default) uses 2.5. One scalar SD applies whole block, mean fixed 0, compiled kernels carry. prior identifies logit level contributes zeros – likelihood monotone coefficient alone send -Inf. sd = Inf removes penalty. Ignored without ziformula. warm_start Optional starting point NUTS sampler, cheaper fit model: "eb" "laplace" fits one first, pass existing fit either mode. sampler starts mode inverse mass read curvature, instead origin structural one. Chains first dispersed around mode fit's scale, -chain spread – rhat() compares – collapsed shared starting point. NUTS/HMC backends take one; rest error rather ignore . available spatial, temporal GP field, whose hyperparameters neither source fit estimates. variance-component slots take adapting mass default, plug-fit estimates curvature . Passing fit tulpa_eb() marginal = TRUE supplies one: theta_cov gives log_sigma_re slot posterior variance start . applies uncorrelated terms, whose hyperparameter coordinates log standard deviations sampler holds; correlated term stays adapting, since log-Cholesky coordinates sampler's. spatial Optional spatial-field spec. addressed depends field family: Areal ("icar", "car", "bym2", "car_proper"): list type adjacency, paired spatial(col) term formula naming per-observation unit column. Term spec must supplied together. Continuous (spatial_gp(~ lon + lat) NNGP field, spatial_gp(~ lon + lat, approx = 'hsgp') Hilbert-space GP, spatial_spde(~ lon + lat, data) Matern SPDE field): spec object carries coordinate columns (SPDE spec also carries mesh + FEM matrices), spatial(col) term used – observations mapped locations coordinates. mode selects spatial hyperparameter handled: mode = "nested_laplace", "structured", "auto" (binomial Gibbs case ) integrate hyperparameter – designed Tier 2 path, mirroring latent(...) blocks. Areal icar/car/ bym2/car_proper continuous gp/nngp/hsgp go tulpa_nested_laplace(); SPDE redirected fit_spde(), integrates (range, sigma) CCD / grid design. mode = "laplace" conditions fixed hyperparameter via tulpa_laplace() (cheap explicit fit). mode = "gibbs" routes areal icar/bym2 cases binomial Polya-Gamma samplers (Tier 1 exact); mode = "auto" picks binomial icar/bym2 field. temporal Optional temporal field spec (temporal_rw1(), temporal_rw2(), temporal_ar1()), integrated nested Laplace. plain field routes single-block temporal kernel; group_var panel spec fits separate walk per group sharing one hyperparameter; combined areal spatial field forms additive space-time joint prior. control Optional list backend tuning arguments (e.g. n_iter, warmup, epsilon mala; n_draws pathfinder). ... what: Soft latent labels go in weights, not in y
title: Fit a latent-variable model via EM + Laplace approximation — tulpa_em_laplace
text: M-step maximizes expected complete-data log-likelihood. Bernoulli latent z_i carrying E-step posterior weight w_i $$Q = \sum_i [\, w_i \log p_i + (1 - w_i) \log (1 - p_i) \,],$$ weighted Bernoulli log-likelihood, carries binomial coefficient. Encode two rows per unit – y = 1 weight w_i y = 0 weight 1 - w_i: fractional y binomial block refused, objective: asks exact binomial density non-integer response, whose normalizer lchoose(n, y) zero depends w. weighted encoding block's log_marginal Laplace marginal Q, EM objective increases across iterations.
code: list(y       = rep(c(1, 0), each = n),      X       = rbind(X, X),      weights = c(w, 1 - w),      family  = "binomial")

title: Fit a latent-variable model via EM + Laplace approximation — tulpa_em_laplace
code: # \donttest{ # Zero-inflated Poisson via EM: the E-step scores the posterior probability # that each zero is non-structural. Those are soft labels, so the occupancy # arm is the weighted Bernoulli above -- two rows per unit -- and the # abundance arm weights each count by the same w. set.seed(1) n <- 200 z <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.7) y <- rpois(n, 4) * z X <- cbind(1, rnorm(n))  e_step <- function(fits, ...) {   if (!length(fits)) return(list(weights = pmax(as.numeric(y > 0), 0.5)))   psi <- plogis(drop(X %*% fits$occ$mode))   lam <- exp(drop(X %*% fits$abund$mode))   w <- ifelse(y > 0, 1, psi * exp(-lam) / (psi * exp(-lam) + (1 - psi)))   list(weights = w) } m_step_encode <- function(weights, ...) {   list(     occ   = list(y = rep(c(1, 0), each = n), X = rbind(X, X),                  weights = c(weights, 1 - weights), family = "binomial"),     abund = list(y = y, X = X, family = "poisson", weights = weights)   ) }  res <- tulpa_em_laplace(e_step, m_step_encode, verbose = FALSE) res$converged #> [1] TRUE plogis(res$fits$occ$mode[1])    # P(non-structural), truth 0.7 #> [1] 0.7041959 exp(res$fits$abund$mode[1])     # abundance mean, truth 4 #> [1] 3.872501 # }

Non-finite values mapped -Inf (cell gets zero weight). beta_mean – numeric vector fixed-effect posterior mean cell. Required combine != "none". beta_cov – p x p numeric matrix fixed-effect marginal covariance cell. Required combine = "law_of_total_cov". hypers named numeric vector current cell's axis values (names match vapply(hyper_specs, [[, character(1), "name")). Errors thrown inner_fit caught treated failed cell (log_marginal = -Inf, beta contribution). combine pool per-cell fixed-effect posteriors single posterior betas. One : "law_of_total_cov" (default) – compute E[Cov(beta | theta)] + Cov(E[beta | theta]) per-cell (beta_mean, beta_cov); synthesise n_draws posterior draws mixture sampling. Requires beta_mean beta_cov per cell. "weighted_mean_only" – pool per-cell beta_mean weighted posterior mean. beta_cov ignored; draws. "none" – assemble fixed-effect posterior. hyperparameter posterior returned. beta_mean / beta_cov inner_fit ignored supplied. n_draws Number posterior draws fixed effects synthesise cell mixture (default 2000). Used combine = "law_of_total_cov". 0 disables draw synthesis (law--total-cov mean covariance still returned). seed Optional integer seed draw synthesis. beta_names Optional character vector naming fixed-effect coordinates. NULL (default) names taken first successful cell's beta_mean (beta1, beta2, ... unnamed). control Optional list refinement / tuning knobs: adaptive_grid (FALSE) – run boundary / interior refinement pass every axis whose spec refinable = TRUE. New cells appended along refining axis paired boundary modal cell's -axis values, carrying marginal-scale calibration contribute right scale. adaptive_grid_edge_thresh (0.02) – per-axis trigger threshold. adaptive_grid_max_passes (1L) – cap refinement passes. var_of_means_consistency (FALSE) – run post-integration consistency pass: refinable axes whose joint-grid var--means undershoots Laplace--mode SD tolerance, append Laplace-guided slice points theta_mean +/- {0.7, 1.5} * theta_sd pinned modal cell. One kernel call per axis. var_of_means_tolerance (0.7) – consistency-pass trigger ratio.

title: Select the symplectic integrator for HMC and NUTS — tulpa_integrator
text: default, "leapfrog", reproduces tulpa's historical trajectory step exactly. "minerror2" two-stage order-two scheme whose coefficient tuned cancel leading energy error Gaussian target. Since mass adaptation drives posterior toward isotropic Gaussian, conserves energy well near adapted optimum adapts larger step sizes, two gradient evaluations per step. recommended choice leapfrog's step size limited energy error near-Gaussian posterior. "yoshida4" order-4 scheme also samples reliably (three gradient evaluations per step). "yoshida6" "yoshida8" available experimental NUTS: high-order composition integrators sharp step-size stability threshold dual-averaging adaptation pushes , "yoshida6" needs high adapt_delta (0.95 ) "yoshida8" often fails adapt. sampling, prefer "leapfrog", "minerror2", "yoshida4". "adaptive2" "adaptive3" step-adapted versions two- three-stage schemes. Rather fixing coefficient advance, NUTS chain resolves end warmup operating point: coefficient minimizes worst-case energy error band dimensionless steps chain actually takes, read adapted mass matrix local posterior curvature. "minerror2" optimal small-step limit, "adaptive2" tracks chain's realised step band; "adaptive3" spends third gradient per step hold small error wider band. run fixed placeholder stage family warmup, dual-averaged step size carries . Step-adaptation applies NUTS (default sampler); fixed-trajectory HMC path uses placeholder. "mts" multiple-time-stepping (RESPA) integrator. splits force stiff cheap prior part – Gaussian latent structure – smooth expensive likelihood part. NUTS trajectory step takes mts_substeps inner leapfrog substeps prior force evaluating likelihood gradient , outer step can larger without stiff prior forcing small. pays one full gradient per step (leapfrog ) plus mts_substeps cheap prior gradients, helps latent field stiff relative comparatively flat likelihood. Like schemes applies NUTS. choice process-global (like gradient mode): set fitting. read main thread start sampling.

Supported priors: Spatial (areal): "icar" (1D grid tau), "bym2" (2D (sigma, rho)), "car_proper" (2D (tau, rho); rho lives eigenvalue interval (1/lambda_min, 1/lambda_max) D^{-1} W). Spatial (continuous): "nngp" (2D (sigma2, phi_gp)), "hsgp" (2D (sigma2, lengthscale)). Temporal: "rw1", "rw2" (1D grid tau), "ar1" (2D (tau, rho)) SPDE continuous spatial: see cpp_nested_laplace_spde() (separate entry, rebuilds Q via SPDE Q-builder).

code: # \donttest{ set.seed(1) S <- 30L                                   # spatial units arranged in a chain nb <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s) setdiff(c(s - 1L, s + 1L), c(0L, S + 1L))) nn <- lengths(nb) field <- as.numeric(scale(cumsum(rnorm(S, 0, 0.4))))   # smooth spatial field idx <- rep(seq_len(S), each = 6L); n <- length(idx); x <- rnorm(n) y <- rbinom(n, 1L, plogis(-0.2 + 0.6 * x + field[idx])) prior <- list(type = "icar", n_spatial_units = S, spatial_idx = idx,               adj_row_ptr = c(0L, cumsum(nn)), adj_col_idx = unlist(nb) - 1L,               n_neighbors = nn, tau_grid = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8)) fit <- tulpa_nested_laplace(y, rep(1L, n), cbind(1, x), prior = prior,                             family = "binomial") fit$theta_mean        # marginalized ICAR precision #> [1] 5.742009 # }

text: Outer-grid nested Laplace driver joint models – multiple response arms sharing one latent prior block, parameterized per-arm field amplitude (sigma) unit-precision latent. code: # \donttest{ set.seed(1) S <- 25L                                   # shared spatial units (chain graph) nb <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s) setdiff(c(s - 1L, s + 1L), c(0L, S + 1L))) nn <- lengths(nb) field <- as.numeric(scale(cumsum(rnorm(S, 0, 0.4)))) mk_arm <- function(m, fam) {   si <- sample(S, m, replace = TRUE); x <- rnorm(m)   lin <- 0.2 + 0.5 * x + 0.8 * field[si]   y <- if (fam == "binomial") rbinom(m, 1L, plogis(lin)) else lin + rnorm(m, 0, 0.5)   list(y = as.numeric(y), n_trials = rep(1L, m), X = cbind(1, x),        spatial_idx = si, family = fam, phi = if (fam == "gaussian") 0.5 else 1) } prior <- list(type = "icar", n_spatial_units = S,               adj_row_ptr = c(0L, cumsum(nn)), adj_col_idx = unlist(nb) - 1L,               n_neighbors = nn, sigma_grid = c(0.3, 0.7, 1.4)) fit <- tulpa_nested_laplace_joint(   responses = list(occ = mk_arm(200L, "binomial"), pos = mk_arm(200L, "gaussian")),   prior = prior) #> [nested-laplace-joint] 1/3 cells (33%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells #> [nested-laplace-joint] 3/3 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells fit$theta_mean        # shared field amplitude, integrated across both arms #>     sigma  #> 0.3147239  # }

title: Fit a beta-regression model via NUTS (joint sampling of beta + log_phi) — tulpa_nuts_beta
text: Bayesian counterpart tulpa_laplace_beta(). Routes Beta GLM tulpa's full NUTS backend via generic LikelihoodSpec interface, sampling precision phi jointly regression coefficients log scale. NUTS performs exact marginalisation phi, replacing Brent outer-opt tulpa_laplace_beta() deterministic nested-Laplace grid otherwise integrate Beta dispersion. Mean-precision parameterisation, default logit link: y_i ~ Beta(mu_i * phi, (1 - mu_i) * phi) mu_i = 1 / (1 + exp(-eta_i)) eta_i = X_i %*% beta.

Unlike agq_fit() (intercept-RE, built-binomial/poisson/gaussian likelihoods), engine callback-driven: caller supplies per-group conditional likelihood, custom marginal (e.g. latent-state-integrated occupancy / detection likelihood, latent-abundance-integrated N-mixture marginal) refines quadrature. engine block, front door: model packages call programmatically, tuning knobs (max_iter, n_quad, keep) sit signature rather control list. engine structure-agnostic. integrates per-group marginal $$M_g = \int \exp\{\ell_g(b_g)\}\, N(b_g; 0, \Sigma)\, db_g,$$ \(b_g\) group's random-effect vector (dimension \(\sum_m c_m\) RE terms) \(\ell_g(b_g)\) group's conditional log-likelihood linear predictors perturbed \(b_g\). \(b_g\) enters likelihood – one linear predictor, several coupled arms different observation granularities (e.g. per-site abundance arm per-visit detection arm sharing species grouping) – lives entirely callback. engine needs, per group, value / gradient / Hessian \(\ell_g\) \(b_g\) (mode) \(\ell_g\) quadrature nodes (sum). fixed parameters theta log-Cholesky coordinates \(\Sigma\) optimized jointly \(\sum_g \log M_g\); standard errors come exact-marginal Hessian. code: # \donttest{ # A per-row-separable binomial GLMM marginal supplied through `make_site`. l1pe <- function(x) ifelse(x > 0, x + log1p(exp(-x)), log1p(exp(x))) make_binom_site <- function(X, y, nt) function(theta) {   eta_fixed <- as.numeric(X %*% theta)   list(eta_re = eta_fixed,        deriv = function(rows, eta) {          p <- plogis(eta)          list(logL = y[rows] * eta - nt[rows] * l1pe(eta),               d1 = y[rows] - nt[rows] * p, d2 = -nt[rows] * p * (1 - p))        },        lmat = function(rows, ETA) y[rows] * ETA - nt[rows] * l1pe(ETA)) } set.seed(1) ng <- 30L; npg <- 8L; n <- ng * npg g <- rep(seq_len(ng), each = npg); x <- rnorm(n) X <- cbind(1, x); nt <- rep(3L, n); u <- rnorm(ng, 0, 0.9) y <- rbinom(n, nt, plogis(0.3 + 0.7 * x + u[g])) fit <- tulpa_re_aghq(theta0 = c(0, 0),                      re_terms = list(list(idx = g, n_groups = ng, n_coefs = 1L)),                      Sigma0 = list(matrix(0.25, 1, 1)),                      make_site = make_binom_site(X, y, nt), n_obs = n, n_quad = 5L) sqrt(fit$Sigma_list[[1]][1, 1])     # adaptive-GHQ RE standard deviation #> [1] 0.796036 # }
